title: Monthly climate, 1991-2020 normals and degree days by city
description:
Monthly climate from February 1950 to December 2025 for the largest cities, with 1991-2020 normals and degree days, computed from the daily ERA5-Land values.

Columns. tmean_c (°C), tmin_mean_c (°C), tmax_mean_c (°C), tmin_abs_c (°C), tmax_abs_c (°C), precip_mm (mm), wet_days (days), frost_days (days), hdd_15_5, hdd_18, cdd_18, cdd_22, gtz_20_15 (degree days, °C·day), solar_kwh_m2 (kWh/m²), wind_mean_kmh (km/h). Normals file 1991-2020 (12 rows per city): tmean_c, tmin_c, tmax_c, precip_mm, wet_days, frost_days, summer_days, hot_days, solar_kwh_m2_day, wind_mean_kmh, hdd_15_5, hdd_18, cdd_18.

Method. Copernicus ERA5-Land hourly reanalysis, 0.1° grid, nearest cell to the city point, local civil days (IANA time zone, complete days only). Temperatures are adjusted for altitude at 6.5 °C per km; precipitation is not adjusted.

Limits. Grid-cell reanalysis values, not station measurements. Daily extremes are smoothed: on record heat days the daily maximum is often 2 to 7 °C below the station record (London, 19 July 2022: 36.4 °C here, 40.2 °C measured at Coningsby). Hot days in city centres are undercounted. Degree days differ from figures published by national services.

Places. France and Germany: the 100 most populous municipalities by official population (France: INSEE population from the "Liste des communes de France" file on data.gouv.fr, Licence Ouverte 2.0; Germany: BKG VG250-EW, © GeoBasis-DE / BKG (2026), dl-de/by-2-0, data changed (climate values added)). One point per municipality (city districts such as the Paris arrondissements are not separate cities); names are the official municipality names; the point and time zone come from GeoNames (cities5000), CC BY 4.0. United Kingdom (100), Portugal (20), Serbia (20) and Luxembourg (5): the most populous GeoNames (cities5000) places, skipping a place that lies in the same 0.1 degree grid cell and district as a larger one. The population column is the official municipal population in France and Germany and the GeoNames population elsewhere; city_id is the GeoNames id. Files are named <cc>_... per country (gb, de, fr, pt, lu, rs).
